XVIII. Sequitur Quintum, de Lege Permissiva
mali: An sit licita, & quatenus? Et an & quate-
nus obligatoria? Ubi imprimis observandum est,
Lege permitti posse rem malam tripliciter: priva-
tive, scilicet, negative & positive. Privative per-
mitti, idem est quo a Legislatore prætermitti, sic
omnia illa permittuntur, de quibus vel prohiben-
dis vel puniendis jura nihil statuunt. Negative
permittitur id, cujus exercitium jura certis limiti-
bus definiunt, intra quos qui se continuerint extra
noxam sunt, qui vero eos excesserint sunt lege pu-
niendi: Sic usuram exerceri permittunt plera-
rumque nationum jura. Positive id permittitur,
cujus, sub certa tributi cujusdam pensione, exer-
citium toleratur. Sic Romæ permittuntur mere-

page.notes: The left edge strip (fragments such as "crupulu", "di neces", "is atten") is the edge of the facing page and is not transcribed. The right-margin numerals are section numbers beside the text: 1. at "Privative permitti", 2. at "Positive id permittitur", 3. at the start of XIX, and 1. and 2. in the margin at "Dico secundò". The numbers are placed in the text as they fall in the margin; their exact line placement is approximate. The word "Permissiva" has a superscript mark over the final a that I could not identify, so I have left it plain. The Q of "Quintum" is an ornamented capital. The catchword "Israelitico" is taken from the foot right and is removed from the text.
